title: Vashti refuses (Esther 1)
hookLine: a queen will not be put on display, and pays for it

lines: THE KING'S HEART MERRY WITH WINE.
SEVEN CHAMBERLAINS SENT FOR THE QUEEN.
cards: The party is in its seventh day. King Ahasuerus has already spent a hundred and eighty days, the text says, showing his officials the riches of his kingdom. Now everyone in the palace city of Shushan is invited.

Wine comes in vessels of gold, as much as each guest pleases. On the seventh day, when the king's heart is merry with wine, he has one more thing to show. He sends seven chamberlains to bring in his queen.

teach.h: TO SHOW HER BEAUTY, LIKE THE TREASURY.
teach.b: The order, in the JPS 1917 translation, was to bring "Vashti the queen before the king with the crown royal, to show the peoples and the princes her beauty; for she was fair to look on."
She's to be brought in and shown, like the gold cups and the rest of the treasury.
Then: "But the queen Vashti refused to come at the king's commandment by the chamberlains; therefore was the king very wroth, and his anger burned in him."
In Hebrew it's quick: vatema'en, and she refused. The text never says why. It gives her no speech.
Just the refusal, in one verb. What follows is almost comic. The king of the whole empire, furious, asks his wise men what the law says to do with a queen who won't come.
One warns that word will spread, and wives across the kingdom will hear and despise their husbands.

So letters go out to every province, to every people in its own language, that every man should bear rule in his own house. Vashti is to come no more before the king, and the search for a new queen begins.
Readers have argued about Vashti for a long time. Some rabbinic stories paint her harshly. Some readers, especially in recent times, see a woman who would not be put on display, and paid for it.
The text itself just sets down her no, and the cost. And it sets the stage: the empty seat beside the king is where the rest of this story will happen.

how: The book of Esther is read aloud from a handwritten scroll on Purim, in the evening and again in the morning, beginning with the king's feast and Vashti's refusal.

o: the queen won't be shown off, and pays for it
the queen refuses to bow before Haman

games.q: vashti said no — tap the pairs.
p: every man to rule his own house

s: the text explains why Vashti refused
it gives her no speech and no reason, only the refusal.
the king asked his wise men what the law said to do
and one warned that wives everywhere would follow her lead.
Vashti's refusal comes near the end of the scroll
it's the opening scene. her empty seat is where the story begins.

games.q: you're Queen Vashti. seven chamberlains arrive: the king wants you brought in, wearing the royal crown, so his guests can see your beauty. what do you do?
o: go, and smile for the guests.
send a gift in your place.
games.why: she refused. the text gives no reason, only her no, and its cost: she was to come no more before the king.

practice: Think of a recent time someone told you no, a friend who couldn't come, a child who wouldn't, a colleague who drew a line, and notice how it felt to hear it, without arguing it again.
Then think of someone whose no you might be pushing against now, and picture letting it stand, without a decree, without making them pay for it. If you pray, ask for the grace to hear no well.

wordCard.voice: Vashti refuses. The queen will not be brought in to be shown off, and the king's anger burns. Today's word.
